newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends slightly higher after late scramble.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends slightly higher after late scramble.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed slightly higher on Wednesday having touched a new session low in the last hour of trade.
Jan Brent ended two cents higher at $23.79 a barrel, having touched an intra-day low of $23.46 in late trade.
"We bounced back again. This market is a survivor, you can't keep it down," said one dealer.
The late dip was in line with NYMEX futures which got the jitters at key resistance levels and fell sharply, having earlier shrugged off bearish EIA inventory data.
The EIA data showed a 200,000 barrel build in crude stocks and a 3.9 million barrel increase in distillate stocks.
"As (NYMEX) heating oil fell the longs started to liquidate, but we still had enough life to come back again," the dealer said.
Analysts said that with Iraq still out of the market, the fundamentals of tight supply are keeping a floor under prices.
Dec gas oil closed earlier up $1.25 a tonne at $224, just 25 cents off the session high. The Dec/Jan backwardation shed $1.25 to end at just $1.50 a tonne.
Brokers said the contract was supported by the strike at France's Elf refineries, now in its seventh day, which is hitting physical volumes in northwest Europe.

After the gas oil close, France's leading trade unions were reported to have called on oil company employees planning disruption on Dec 10 to widen their protests to a full one-day oil industry strike.
